svg.title: A due date drawn over the epic’s name — SoftTrack web design mockup (#319)
svg.desc: On a board card with both an epic and a due date, the date is drawn over the end of the epic’s name once the card is about 200px wide. The fix lets the chip shorten with an ellipsis, so the date and the avatar keep their place at every width the board can produce.
svg.text: A due date drawn over the epic’s name
· the chip gives way, the date stays whole
Today: six columns at 1440px, and the date sits on the name
signed in as Amina, on the Engineering board
the date and avatar stay put
The date and the avatar stay
. The list view and the peek
draw the same badge and get the same check.
Done when the chip shortens at every card width the board can produce, the full epic name is still available to a pointer and a screen reader, the list view and the peek are
checked, and a test pins the narrow case, since it looks fine on a wide board.

g.text: An overdue date overlaps the same
way, and it is the date that most needs
17px of the two are drawn in the same
The card is 194px wide; the chip’s text
ends at 618px and the date starts at 601px.
The name ends in an ellipsis. The whole of it stays on the chip for
a pointer and for a screen reader.
Chips take the width that is left and wrap under each other.
Nothing is drawn under the date at any width.
